text: dsh-opencli 是面向 DSH 的浏览器自动化工具插件，通过注册工具直接连接本机 OpenCLI daemon。它提供 JavaScript 表达式执行、页面导航与结构快照，并支持标签页、截图、Cookie、网络记录、文件上传和文本输入等浏览器操作。工具使用配置的默认会话访问持久化自动化标签页；适合需要在 DSH 中查看和操作浏览器页面的场景。运行时需要本机 OpenCLI daemon 与浏览器扩展；插件默认连接 127.0.0.1:19825，无需 API key。

dsh-opencli connects DSH to the local OpenCLI daemon for browser automation. It runs JavaScript, navigates and summarizes pages, manages tabs, captures screenshots and network activity, reads cookies, uploads files and enters text. It requires the local daemon and browser extension.
想让 DSH 直接操作我已经登录的浏览器页面。
有没有办法在 DSH 里导航网页并查看页面结构？
I want DSH to inspect and interact with pages in my local browser.
dsh-opencli 的功能「页面操作」：通过本机 daemon 执行 JavaScript、导航网页并返回页面信息；调用 oc_exec、oc_navigate 或 oc_snapshot。
dsh-opencli 的功能「标签页与浏览器辅助操作」：提供标签页管理、截图、Cookie 查询、网络记录、文件上传和文本输入等工具；调用相应 oc_* 工具并指定会话及所需参数。

dsh-opencli README · dsh-opencli：Low-latency browser tools for DSH that drive the **local OpenCLI daemon directly** instead of spawning the `opencli` CLI once per command.

[](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-opencli)
[](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-opencli)
[](LICENSE)

dsh-opencli README · dsh-opencli：`opencli` pays a Node cold start on every call — it resolves 318 modules to send one request (~1.4–1.8 s per command; measured: `opencli list search` = 1071 ms). The daemon, once warm, answers the same request in **5–20 ms**. This plugin keeps that daemon as a resident service: it posts to `http://127.0.0.1:19825/command` with the `X-OpenCLI: 1` header and hands the result straight back to the agent.

dsh-opencli README · dsh-opencli：```
CLI path    : agent -> shell -> node opencli -> (318 modules) -> daemon   ~1400-1800 ms
plugin path : agent -> oc_exec -> fetch()     ->                daemon    ~10-20 ms
```

dsh-opencli README · Install：Published on npm: **[dsh-opencli](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-opencli)** (registry: `https://registry.npmjs.org/dsh-opencli`, `npm view dsh-opencli version` for the current release).

**A · Inside DSH** — let the plugin manager resolve it from the registry:

```bash
plugin_manager action=install_bundle target=dsh-opencli
```

From a checkout instead: `plugin_manager action=install_bundle target=/absolute/path/to/dsh-opencli`.

dsh-opencli README · Install：**B · With the `dsh` CLI** — the CLI's `plugin` command forwards the rest of the line to pnpm inside that profile directory:

```bash
npx @deepseek-ai/dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-opencli   # or install it once: npm i -g @deepseek-ai/dsh
```

**C · Manually, with npm / pnpm** — a DSH profile is an ordinary package directory, so the plugin is an ordinary dependency:

dsh-opencli README · Install：```bash
cd ~/.dsh/profiles/web          # the profile you run; `web` is the desktop default
pnpm add dsh-opencli            # or: npm install dsh-opencli
```

Profiles created by the desktop app carry a pnpm `.npmrc` (`node-linker=hoisted`), so prefer `pnpm add` there; plain `npm install dsh-opencli` also works in a profile that has no pnpm setup. Behind a mirror: append `--registry=https://registry.npmmirror.com`.

dsh-opencli README · Install：⚠️ **B and C only install the package** — neither touches `dsh.profile.bundles`, so the harness will not load it until you enable the bundle (the sidebar's **Plugins** page, which both installs and selects; or the `plugin_manager` tool when your preset enables it). Route A does that step for you. Also keep the pnpm doing the install in step with the profile's lockfile: a v9 lockfile needs pnpm 10+, and an older pnpm prints `Ignoring broken lockfile ... not compatible with current pnpm` and re-resolves the whole profile (the desktop app ships its own pnpm 11.8 for exactly this reason).

dsh-opencli README · Tools：| Tool | What it does | Writes |
|---|---|---|
| `oc_status` | Daemon version, online state, extension connection, contextId, profiles, memory. The first call when something breaks. | no |
| `oc_exec` | Runs JS expressions in your already-logged-in browser. `codes` runs up to 40 expressions in one round trip; evaluation is async, so `await fetch(...)` works. | depends |
| `oc_navigate` | Opens a URL, waits for load, returns title / final URL / whether it timed out. | yes |
| `oc_snapshot` | Compresses the page into a compact interactive structure (title, links with href, buttons, inputs with name/placeholder, disabled flags) — an order of magnitude cheaper than `outerHTML`. | no |
| `oc_tabs` | `list` / `new` / `select` / `close` tabs inside the automation container. | new/select/close |
| `oc_screenshot` | Captures the viewport (or full page) to a PNG/JPEG file under the system temp dir and returns its path. | no |
| `oc_cookies` | Reads cookies for one domain/URL scope — the logged-in session of the real browser. | no |
| `oc_network` | `start` / `read` a network capture buffer: URL, method, request headers, response status, body preview. | start/read |

dsh-opencli README · Tools：`session` is the key of a persistent automation tab (default `dsh`), so different jobs get isolated tabs for free. Every `oc_tabs` op takes a session (falls back to the configured default).

dsh-opencli README · Coverage：The tool set mirrors what the OpenCLI **daemon** can do, because that is the fast path (5–20 ms) and the CLI's own sub-commands are only reachable by paying its 1.4–1.8 s cold start:

dsh-opencli README · Coverage：- Covered here: expression evaluation, navigation, tab management, snapshots, screenshots, cookies, network capture, file upload, text input, frames, whitelisted CDP calls, native Chrome tab/group/window management, window/tab closing, and download waiting.
- Not covered here: the OpenCLI **site adapters** (176 of them — GitHub, Xiaohongshu, Twitter, …) and the CLI-only browser verbs (`click`, `fill`, `scroll`, `dialog`, …). Those run inside the `opencli` CLI process, not behind the daemon, so wrapping them here would reintroduce the cold start this plugin exists to avoid. Drive them with the `opencli` CLI directly, or use `oc_exec` / `oc_cdp` against the same page.

dsh-opencli README · Coverage：`oc_cdp` is restricted to a whitelist of CDP methods (`DOM.*`, `Page.captureScreenshot`, `Input.dispatchMouseEvent`, `Runtime.enable`, …); `Runtime.evaluate` is denied by the extension, so use `oc_exec` for JavaScript.

`oc_chrome` operates the browser's **native** tabs, groups and windows — not the automation container. Native tabs survive after the session ends, so treat `oc_chrome op=call` as a user-visible write.

dsh-opencli README · Config：Three fields in `cordis.patch.yml`, overridable from the profile patch or the plugin settings UI:

```yaml
config:
  port: 19825          # must match `opencli daemon status`
  defaultSession: dsh  # session key for the persistent automation tab
  timeoutMs: 30000     # per-expression budget, clamped to 2000-120000

dsh-opencli README · Troubleshooting：| Symptom | Fix |
|---|---|
| `daemon_unreachable` | `opencli daemon restart` (any `opencli` command also auto-starts it) |
| `extension ... disconnected` | Open the OpenCLI extension in Chrome/Edge, keep that browser window alive, re-check `extensionConnected` in `opencli daemon status` |
| `Page is not in the automation container` | `select` only reaches tabs inside the container: open one with `op=new` first |
| `page_not_found` / `stale page identity` | `oc_tabs op=list` for the current `index`/`page`, or omit `page` and let the daemon choose |
| `ReferenceError` / `SyntaxError` | The expression itself is wrong: call `oc_snapshot` first and look at what the DOM really contains |
| `Cookie scope required` | `oc_cookies` needs a `domain` or `url`; the daemon refuses an unscoped cookie dump on purpose |
| `CDP method not permitted` | `oc_cdp` only allows whitelisted methods; `Runtime.evaluate` is one of the blocked ones — use `oc_exec` |
| `No element found matching selector` | The `oc_upload` selector does not match on the current page — check it with `oc_snapshot` first |
| download never arrives | `oc_download` waits for a real download; if

dsh-opencli README · Troubleshooting：Every failure comes back as a structured value, not a throw: `{ ok: false, errorCode, error, hint }` — `hint` names the next action. A dead daemon is deliberately **not** auto-restarted, so a real outage never hides behind a silent retry.

dsh-opencli README · Safety：These tools drive your **real** browser with your real logins — clicks, form fills and closed tabs happen in the window in front of you. For simple, unauthenticated page tests prefer headless Playwright; reach for `oc_*` when you actually need a logged-in session or a persistent tab.

dsh-opencli README · Development：`index.js` is a host-side module: editing it does **not** hot-reload. Re-import it by toggling the plugin entry.

```
plugin_manager action=list_plugins                                        # find include:dsh-opencli
plugin_manager action=set_plugin target=include:dsh-opencli enabled=false
plugin_manager action=set_plugin target=include:dsh-opencli enabled=true
```

dsh-opencli README · Development：The harness validates each tool's `output.schema` strictly (`additionalProperties: false`), so one undeclared field fails the whole call with `tool "oc_xxx" returned invalid output`. That only shows up on a real invocation — never in a direct `execute()` call — so `npm test` validates real outputs against the declared schemas:

```bash
npm test        # schema conformance: success envelopes, failure envelopes, daemon-down
```
